best_for: PlayStation 1 fans with their own discs and console BIOS who want sharper 3D, save states and achievements on a Windows or Linux PC.

points.title: Bring your own BIOS
points.text: No game starts until you add a PS1 or PS2 BIOS file, and none is included. The project says to dump it from a console you own. Any region works, though a BIOS from another region can upset some games.

points.title: Sharper than the original
points.text: The hardware renderers can upscale, use 24-bit color and filter textures. PGXP fixes the wobbly geometry and warped textures PS1 games are known for, so old 3D games look steadier on a modern screen.

points.title: Rewind, runahead and achievements
points.text: Save states come with rewind and runahead. RetroAchievements is built in. It also supports light guns such as the GunCon, the NeGcon, and multitap for up to 8 controllers.

points.title: Reads the disc images you already have
points.text: It plays real CDs and bin/cue, CHD, ECM, MDS/MDF, CCD and unencrypted PBP images. CHD files save the most space.

points.title: Free, but not open in the usual sense
points.text: DuckStation costs nothing, but its CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license bars commercial use and modified copies. Shipping it with preset settings counts as a modification. Windows needs Windows 10 version 1809 or later; Windows 7 and 8 are not supported.

points.title: The Flatpak is not the author's
points.text: The Flathub page now calls its package community-provided and not supported by the developer. The project's own Linux builds are AppImages, and its README explains how to move data from the Flatpak to the AppImage.

points.title: A short version history here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 6 versions as portable zip files for x64 and Arm64. Linux lists only the current release, so older builds need the GitHub releases page. The project also makes Mac builds, which are not listed here.
